data.description:
The rule "a plan review that PASSED but whose attestation failed to persist is RETRYABLE, not
success" exists only in the CLI: `_cli/_llm_commands.py:129-171` inspects `result["signature"]`,
discriminates `plan_review_generation_changed` vs `plan_review_sign_aborted` vs transient, and
returns exit 11.

`_mcp_llm.py:227-229` returns `rebar.llm.review_plan(...)` raw, with no such inspection. Verified
end-to-end: an MCP agent sees `verdict: PASS`, proceeds to `claim`, and the claim gate refuses
because the signature the gate consumes was never written.

The surface most used by autonomous agents has the weaker implementation. The recovery
(`sign_review`) IS already exposed over MCP — the agent simply is not told to use it. This is a
presentation gap in the seam, not a missing capability.

Both proposers converged on extracting the classifier below both front-ends.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The retryable/cause discrimination lives in one place below CLI and MCP
- [ ] The CLI still maps it to exit 11 with byte-identical stderr
- [ ] The MCP result carries a structured retryable flag and names `sign_review` as the recovery
- [ ] A test covers the passed-but-unsigned state on both surfaces
data.title: Hoist the passed-but-unsigned classifier below CLI and MCP
